scope: Proposition 3.7 (Joint spatial bounds) of the manuscript “Ground-state condensation in the dilute hard-sphere gas” (preprints/Ground-state-condensation-in-the-dilute-hard-sphere-gas-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 267 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3f861f3b57ec1d6a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every A ⊂ L, log ∫︂ ezfA dµ ≤ CzD|A| (0 ≤ z ≤ 1), (3.18) where f∅ = 0. Fix any θ > 0. One can choose b > 0 sufficiently small depending on θ, then take D sufficiently large, so that the random site set Q(X) = {v ∈ L : #{i : d(xi, v) ≤ 5, di ≤ s0} ≥ θD} (3.19) satisfies µ{A ⊂ Q} ≤ p |A| D , pD = (︂ Cθb−2 D−4/3 )︂1/Q −→ 0. (3.20) Here Q is an absolute integer; D is taken large enough that the displayed base is at most one. All statements are uniform for α ∈ [α0/2, 2α0], K ≥ 100, and the ground function.
